newsitem.title: UK: British water users lobby raps Severn Trent.
newsitem.headline: British water users lobby raps Severn Trent.

text.p: A regional British water customer lobby group has rapped Severn Trent Water for underspending on its capital investment and said any savings should be shared between customers and shareholders.

In a letter to Severn Trent, Clive Wilkinson, the chairman of the Central area Customer Service Committee (CSC) of industry watchdog Ofwat, defended his alleagation that the company was "underspending on (its) capital programme."
He added that any reduction in the company's costs would be considered as efficiency savings and should be shared with customers and shareholders.

Wilkinson, replying to a letter from Severn Trent chairman Brian Duckworth, said Severn Trent was some 100 million stg behind an 800 million stg target of investment for the first two years of a five year period.
"This is well behind, at this stage of the programme, what any efficiency savings would allow."
He went on to criticise Severn Trent's claim of "additional" expenditure of around 244 million stg, saying that it was "replacing planned expenditure...with so-called additional expenditure."
Wilkinson said the company should be investing to improve services to customers and that the CSC would monitor Severn Trent's capital expenditure programme.
"I believe Ofwat's view on what is a proper return to shareholders in a low risk industry like water is somewhat more modest than Severn Trent's view," Wilkinson said.
